analysis.title: GS Privorotsky - GS Basics Tech Rotation. FCF Inflection. Labor/AI
key_insights: Samsung disappointed, mainly on the lack of shareholder returns against a higher bar set after Hynix. Advantest rose sharply on a significant guidance upgrade, which Privorotsky reads as another sign of robust AI demand.
The hyperscaler earnings tape was messy on headlines but compute trajectory remains robust. One mega cap platform fell about 10% after hours on consumer ad misses while Cloud growth stayed strong.

The second hyperscaler print was cleaner: core cloud beat whispers, quarterly FCF was positive and total contracted obligations expanded. The light capex outlay reflected third-party facility delivery timing, not reduced appetite, and next quarter is guided higher.

Aggregate spending intentions across both hyperscalers are flat to higher, with power and cluster delivery the main bottlenecks. The market has moved past questioning capex durability to asking about value capture: whether cheaper model running benefits hyperscaler returns on capital or expands enterprise application gross margins.

Oracle is called arguably the most important development for credit. The stock rallied double digits after management outlined positive FCF in H2 FY28 and $30bn+ in FY29, with capex stepping down in FY29 and incremental capital raises capped at $20bn through FY30 excluding refinancing.

Oracle guided to non-GAAP operating margins of 40%+ by FY30 on $225 billion+ revenue, with high-20s project returns on a fully ramped gigawatt and about $16bn annualized revenue per gigawatt. This is not a capex cut but an attempt to show the economics work and the funding cycle ends. It depends on execution, utilization and financing, and spreads have yet to respond.

Fed: Privorotsky found Warsh balanced, with early references to tightening financial conditions. There were two hawkish dissents (Cook and Hammack), Logan did not dissent, growth assessment was upgraded and inflation is still elevated. December still looks like a hike with little reason for material repricing. The event was volatility-suppressing.

ECB: Two hikes since June, with the question whether December brings a third. French sovereign stress is adding tightening. With European gas near €100/MWh, a dovish pivot is unlikely, though some repricing is possible if financial conditions get more airtime.

Energy/geopolitics: Vance's letter to Iran looks like a last-minute bid for a diplomatic win, but Iran shows no sign of capitulating. Privorotsky sees the path leading toward post-midterm escalation and notes European equities are looking through €100 gas and elevated oil.

Risk: The pain trade is hyperscalers underperforming while de-risked picks and shovels work. Credit is the key watch item, with Oracle potentially more consequential for levered infrastructure than either hyperscaler print. The market is shifting from rewarding capex growth to demanding evidence of returns. Privorotsky expects dips to be bought.
